assumptions: Host-directed correction of the existing Periastra Meridian archive. Exactly two defects are repaired - the off-centre yoke arms and the board's missing fit layer - and nothing else in the object moves.

The name is kept. The correction brief says so in terms: this is a correction to Periastra Meridian, not a new toy. The distinct revision identity is carried in the documentation as revision C, not in the customer-facing title.
The two counters are frozen byte for byte and their sha256 are asserted in measure/check_fit.py, which fails the build if either moves.
RECESS 0.8, SQUARE_BEVEL 0.3 and SQUARE_CORNER 1.5 are the mechanism section B of the brief replaces and are removed entirely; check_fit.py asserts they are absent from the library.

Every other listed constant keeps its value; the closed object stays 190 x 190 x 110.7, the dome stays an exact hemisphere on a visible drum, and the telescope stays exactly where it is. Only the yoke arms move, and only in x.
Two known defects - the open perimeter reveal and the loose gravity-seated inlays - are scoped out by the host and recorded as one disclosed limitation rather than repaired.

build_plan.exit_criteria: Each of the five distinct designs passes its own isolated build, wall and visual round before the combined entry is reviewed; part_sun_counter.step and part_moon_counter.step reproduce their frozen sha256 byte for byte; the built roof measures mirror-symmetric about x=0 under 1 mm3 and its yoke arms slice at |x| 5.000 to 9.000 at three heights; the board's built void matches exactly 32 chamfered 22.0 mm pockets at the dark-cell centres, blind on 9.0 mm of backing, with 21.5 mm inlays flush to within 0.05 mm and a closed manifold mesh; all 58 occurrences export as named single solids; STEP export is reproducible run to run; and one independent critic reads the canonical images, including a straight-down frame cropped to the slit and the populated and empty board at whole-board scale, before learning what the object is.

components.duty: Carry all 24 counters and support the removable roof.
components.form: 190 by 190 by 24 mm rounded square solid-bottom plinth; 3 mm perimeter walls drop to z17 along the open side spans, retaining z24 corner piers. 176 mm 8x8 board on a floor at z11, 22 mm cells. The 32 cells where file + rank is even carry a BLIND pocket 22.0 mm across and 2.0 mm deep with all four plan corners chamfered 1.0 mm, on 9.0 mm of continuous backing - the house tiled-board fit layer, scaled to this 22 mm square. The old 0.8 mm recess with its 0.3 mm sloped lip and 1.5 mm rounded corners is gone. Two 3 mm half-disc orientation marks on the mid-file edges, unchanged and untouched.
components.interfaces: 184 mm square inner opening; four integral 3 by 3 mm corner ledges from floor z11 to top z21 seat the roof plate with 0.8 mm lateral clearance per side. Each of the 32 pockets takes one inlay with 0.25 mm of clearance per side; the inlay top finishes flush with the board floor at z11.
components.name: Observatory board base
components.placement: Centred on x=y=0; bottom z=0; floor z=11; board spans -88 to 88 on x and y.

components.duty: Close and store the populated board, and read unmistakably as an observatory when it is lifted clear.
components.form: 182.4 mm square backing plate 3.0 mm thick with 1.2 mm corners, flat underside, no notches, cut-outs or holes. A visible 150 mm drum of radius 75.0 and height 11.7 stands on it, carrying one rotation-ring seam 2.0 mm along the axis by 1.0 mm deep, centred 4.0 mm below the drum top, its upper wall relieved at 50 degrees. An EXACT HEMISPHERE of radius 75.0, centred on the axis at the drum top, rises from there: base radius 75.0, rise 75.0, so at its base the dome surface is vertical and flows continuously into the drum wall. One 30.0 mm shutter slit with parallel square-cut walls is cut on a single meridian in the YZ plane, open from the bottom of the drum, up over the apex and 30.0 mm of surface arc (22.9 degrees) down the far side, so the far half of the dome is unbroken. A slender telescope stands in the slit on x = 0: 15.0 mm outer tube, 45.0 mm long, 35 degrees above horizontal, with an open 7.0 mm muzzle bore 13.0 mm deep leaving a 4.0 mm tube wall. It is carried on a yoke of two 4.0 mm arms, arm A spanning x = -9.000 to -5.000 and arm B spanning x = +5.000 to +9.000, measured on the built STEP: 6.000 mm of clear air to each slit wall, equal both sides, a 10.000 mm gap between them centred on x = 0, and 2.500 mm of overlap with the tube's own x range so both arms carry it. The pair is produced by building one arm, placing it by its measured bounding box and MIRRORING it, a construction that cannot depend on extrusion winding order; the whole roof measures mirror-symmetric about x = 0 at 0.0000 mm3. They rise rising from a solid pier that is fused to the drum, with a keel that carries the tube to its muzzle so nothing is cantilevered. The flat plate margin round the dome is 16.2 mm and is bare: no railing, walkway, ladder, panelling, ribs, rivets, windows, finial or decoration of any kind.
components.interfaces: Flat plate underside rests on the four base ledges at z21. No skirt, hinge, latch, magnet or hardware of any kind, and no assembly step. Lifts straight up 100 mm to reveal the board.
components.name: Observatory dome roof
components.placement: Seated: plate underside at z21, drum z24 to z35.7, dome apex z110.7, telescope muzzle 13.0 mm clear of the dome surface.

components.duty: One dark square of the chequerboard. The board is printed opaque in one colour per part, so the square is a separate part in a contrasting filament rather than a step in the floor.
components.form: Flat square tile 21.5 x 21.5 x 2.0 mm with all four PLAN corners chamfered 1.0 mm - faceted, not rounded. No draft, relief, boss, hole or retention feature of any kind. The chamfers are the baseline's structural detail: they leave a 1.414 mm material bridge where two diagonally adjacent pockets meet, which is what closes the board mesh.
components.interfaces: Drops into a blind 22.0 mm pocket 2.0 mm deep in the board floor, 0.25 mm of clearance per side, gravity-seated with no retention feature, top flush with the board floor at z11. concept.interaction: Lift the roof 100 mm straight up and set it aside. Play English draughts unchanged: men move and capture diagonally forward one square, capture is compulsory, a man reaching the far row is crowned and its turn ends there, a king moves and captures one square diagonally in all four directions. Crown by stacking one of your own captured counters on the promoted piece. When the game ends, return the counters to their dark cells and lower the roof back onto the four ledges.
concept.print_stance: Base bottom down. Roof flat backing plate down with the dome apex up, so the hemisphere is self-supporting from its vertical base and the telescope rests on its own keel. Counters flat on either face - the two faces are identical, so the choice is free; the bed contact is the 2.0 mm rim band plus the coplanar flat top of the raised symbol.
risks: check_overhang still fails both counters on its connected-region span proxy: the field floor is one connected ring, so the proxy reports the full 14.0 mm field diameter against a 12 mm allowance. Measured free bridge 2.40 mm on the Sun and 9.75 mm on the Moon. The counters are FROZEN by this correction and could not be redesigned even if it were wanted; the product is sealed digitally-verified-not-print-ready and makes no print-ready claim.

Because two print entries fail a print gate, the assembled-object make_round was run without --require-component-passes. Every one of the five designs still had its own isolated round; base, inlay and roof pass outright, and the two counters pass build, wall and visual and fail only the proxy above. No threshold was lowered and the failure is reported unchanged at every level.

The diagonal material bridge between two chamfered pockets measures 1.414 mm, below the 3 mm minimum feature width the rest of this set observes. It is a 2.0 mm ridge fused along its whole length to a continuous 9.0 mm slab, not a freestanding feature, and check_thickness passes part_base at a 0.4 mm nozzle. The baseline's own gate-passed product carries the same detail at 1.482 mm when scaled to this square, so this is 4.55 % under that proportion, all of it from rounding the chamfer from 1.048 to 1.0. Disclosed rather than engineered away.

The 32 inlays are loose and the closed box has an open 4.0 mm perimeter reveal. An inlay is 2.0 mm thick and can leave through it; a counter is 7.0 mm thick and cannot. The host scoped both out of this revision, so they are recorded together as one disclosed limitation and neither is attempted.

concept.signature_decision: A 150 mm hemispherical observatory dome, split by one shutter slit with a bored telescope standing CENTRED in it on a symmetric two-arm yoke, lifts straight off a populated draughts board whose dark squares are inlaid tiles in a second colour. The dome is the lid; the reveal is the whole toy. Both of this revision's repairs serve the same thing - that the object reads correctly to someone looking straight at it, rather than only from a flattering angle.
concept.summary: English draughts - an observatory theme: the Sun side and the Moon side meet across an inlaid chequerboard, and the dome that watches them is the lid of the box.
concept.title: Periastra Meridian

design_changes.change: Yoke arms rebuilt by mirroring: arm A spans x = -9.000 to -5.000 and arm B spans x = +5.000 to +9.000, 6.000 mm of clear air to each slit wall, a 10.000 mm gap centred on x = 0, and 2.500 mm of overlap with the tube on each side.
design_changes.previous: Both arms 4.000 mm off centre at [-13.000, -9.000] and [+1.000, +5.000]: one lone fin standing beside the tube without touching it, and one arm buried inside the tube's x range carrying the telescope by itself off its centreline.
design_changes.reason: Host correction. The cause was that extrude() takes its direction from the face normal, which follows the polygon winding order; arm_profile() winds so the normal points at -x, so extrude(face, 4.0) spanned x = -4.000 to 0.000 and both hand-written offsets landed 4 mm low. The arm is now placed by its MEASURED bounding box and the second is a mirror of the first, so the construction cannot depend on winding order. The reason is written into the source as a comment.

design_changes.change: measure/check_fit.py now cuts the built part_roof.step against its own mirror image about x = 0 and fails the build above 1 mm3 of asymmetric volume, and slices the roof at z = 18, 25 and 32 to assert the arm lumps at |x| 5.000 to 9.000 within 0.01 mm.
design_changes.previous: No symmetry gate existed. Every telescope frame in the evidence set was oblique, and at an oblique angle a fin beside the tube looks like an arm cradling it, so the defect survived a full review.
design_changes.reason: This is the gate that would have caught the shipped defect. Measured: the archive roof leaves 8987.8055 mm3 (0.9119 %) of 985625.9 mm3; this revision leaves 0.0000 mm3.

design_changes.change: The board's 32 dark cells are the house tiled-board FIT LAYER: blind 22.0 mm pockets 2.0 mm deep with 1.0 mm plan corner chamfers on 9.0 mm of continuous backing, each holding a separate 21.5 x 2.0 mm inlay at 0.25 mm clearance per side, finishing flush and printed in a contrasting filament. 32 new printed parts and one new geometry family.
design_changes.previous: 32 cells recessed RECESS 0.8 mm with a SQUARE_BEVEL 0.3 mm sloped lip and SQUARE_CORNER 1.5 mm rounded corners, in one colour. A blind critic read the floor as random staggered brickwork rather than a board.
design_changes.reason: Host correction, and the Mara Masque skill makes references/tiled-board-baseline.md mandatory for a tiled board with standing pieces; it had never been read for this product. Geometry alone cannot fix it: the set prints opaque one colour per part and the evidence renderer shades from the surface normal alone, so two flat horizontal faces at different heights come out the same tone. The baseline's answer is separate parts in a contrasting colour, which SKILL.md permits in terms.

design_changes.change: Pocket depth 2.0 mm and inlay thickness 2.0 mm, overriding the baseline's 2.6 mm.
design_changes.previous: Baseline default 2.6 mm, set by a 5.0 mm playing surface over a 2.4 mm backing.
design_changes.reason: This board's floor is 11.0 mm, so depth is free. 2.0 mm is ten layers at 0.2 mm, enough to seat the inlay without making the pocket a well, and it leaves 9.0 mm of continuous backing against the baseline's 2.4 mm minimum.

design_changes.change: Inlay 21.5 mm against a 22.0 mm pocket - the baseline's 0.5 mm total straight-edge clearance carried UNSCALED.
design_changes.previous: Baseline 41.5 mm inlay in a 42 mm pocket.
design_changes.reason: 0.5 mm total is a fit tolerance, not a proportion. Shrinking it with the square would be wrong. The clearance was not tightened toward interference to stop the inlays falling out: the baseline states the limit of its own evidence and the host accepted the consequence.

design_changes.change: Corner chamfer 1.0 mm, applied to every inlay corner and every internal pocket corner, replacing SQUARE_CORNER's 1.5 mm rounding.
design_changes.previous: Baseline 2.0 mm at a 42 mm square; this product had a 1.5 mm ROUNDING serving the same bridging purpose.
design_changes.reason: Scaled with the square (2.0 x 22/42 = 1.048, rounded to 1.0). A chamfer rather than a round because the baseline says to prefer faceted recesses to circular ones in small detail. The chamfers are structural: they leave a 1.414 mm material bridge at each diagonal junction and the board mesh closes, which check_fit.py proves by tessellating the built base and finding every directed edge used exactly once.

design_changes.change: The baseline clause that pocket corners open square at panel seams is deliberately NOT used.
design_changes.previous: Baseline: square corners at panel seams, because chamfering there leaves thin tapering wedges that fail a wall-thickness check.
design_changes.reason: That clause exists because Civic Skyline is a 384 mm board quartered to fit a 220 mm bed. This board is a single 176 mm field on a 190 mm base and has no seams, so there is no seam corner to open square. Every pocket corner gets its chamfer.

design_changes.change: Counters now seat on the flush inlay top at z11.0 rather than in a 0.8 mm recess at z10.2, so the storage void is exactly FLOOR 11.0 to LEDGE_TOP 21.0 = 10.0 mm against a 7.0 mm counter: 3.0 mm clear.
design_changes.previous: A 10.8 mm void with 3.8 mm clear, because the counter sat 0.8 mm down in the recess.
design_changes.reason: The inlays finish flush, so they consume zero of the storage void. Measured on the built base rather than asserted: board floor z11.000, pocket floor z9.000, ledge top z21.000.

design_changes.change: Delivered part count 26 to 58, geometry families 4 to 5.
design_changes.reason: One printed inlay per dark square, as the baseline's fit layer requires and the host chose. measure/revision_diff.py asserts that every archive part key is still present and that the only additions are inlay_01..inlay_32.

design_changes.previous: No hash gate on the counters.

research.novelty_assessment: Carried forward unchanged: a bounded search found adjacent printed checkers-and-storage products, not proof of worldwide novelty. The claim is an unusual original combination, not a first. This revision repairs two defects and introduces no new claim.
research.popularity_assessment: Carried forward unchanged from the source set's sealed research: two independent cited sources corroborate household-scale and enduring recognition of English draughts. This correction changes no rule, no component function and no source game, so it reopens no popularity question; the citations and their access dates are the originals.
research.rights_assessment: Carried forward unchanged: traditional public-domain game mechanics, with independently authored rule prose and geometry. WCDF document expression is not copied or represented as public domain.

sources.claim: WCDF 2012 section 1 is the frozen source for gameplay and adjudication. Original prose and physical expression will not be copied. Tournament dimensions differ from the explicitly requested miniature equipment.
The Strong records induction in 2003 and reports Pressman's estimate of more than 25 million sets sold since 1922, supporting enduring widespread recognition.
Independent Board Game Central describes American/standard checkers as the most commonly played checkers in the United States. Its simplified rules are not used as this product's rules authority.
Traditional checkers adaptation is explicitly designated Public Domain. This corroborates traditional-game lineage; it does not release WCDF document prose.

US Copyright Office distinguishes unprotected ideas, systems and methods from protected expression. Only traditional gameplay mechanics are implemented, with independently authored text and geometry; no claim that WCDF publication is public domain.
NASA describes comet trajectories changing through gravity and ejection by gravitational encounters. Periastra uses these as a spatial metaphor, not a physical orbital simulation.
Nearby printed space-checkers listing; fetched title establishes proximity but no detailed rules/form claims can be made from its empty body.
Designer describes a sliding board retained by a lip. Periastra has a permanent floor and vertically removed conical roof instead.
